items.summary: CTO review: preserve containment and admit no new implementation while delivery is saturated at 10/10 active slots. The candidate control-plane improvement is technically feasible in principle, but it is not safe to queue now: current evidence shows no available capacity, repeated duplicate/stranded work, failed requests, and incomplete execution linkage. Do not infer that a new deduplication system will reduce triage time or improve reliability without an isolated prototype and measured outcome.

After one slot is released, admit only the existing canonical allthingsmasonic.com CTA refinement. Keep scope to one isolated site change, deterministic tests, destination and tracking-ID validation, disclosure/accessibility checks, and single-diff rollback. Measure outbound affiliate clicks against the recorded 61-click baseline; retain ordered items and commission as secondary fields without revenue, ROI, or causal claims.

Reject or defer the proposed fleet-wide admission/deduplication implementation, AI-cost guardrails, work-graph expansion, site-factory builds, CRO prototypes, and new telemetry requests this cycle. A control-plane change would require an isolated worktree or disposable control-plane fixture, explicit idempotency and capability tests, queue/measurement/rollback linkage tests, failure recovery validation, owner-approved implementation, and a measurable baseline. Existing operational and fleet-doctor evidence is incomplete, so no reliability or isolation claim is currently supportable.

Keep private-launch and security-sensitive release gates unchanged. Do not add dependencies, credentials, permissions, cross-site behavior, production configuration, external outreach, or public exposure. The strongest site-factory candidate remains preview-only and cannot enter the implementation queue until launch-readiness, compliance, security, measurement, owner, and rollback evidence exists.
